title: Routing rule verifier and migration adapter for tier/region fallback policies
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background: The policy runtime currently allows a mix of ad-hoc routing rules that express region preference, customer tier routing, and fallback model variants. Over time the ruleset has accumulated incompatible shapes which lead to surprising dispatch behavior during capacity pressure and failover (region fallthroughs that choose higher-cost variants, incorrect tier isolation).

Goal: Implement a validator and a migration adapter that: (1) enforces a stable, expressive config schema (DSL) for routing rules covering region selection, tier routing, and fallback model variants; (2) provides a safe migration path for existing configs; and (3) integrates into the policy compiler with clear errors, warnings, and fix suggestions.

Scope / Deliverables:
- A JSON/YAML schema for the routing DSL (versioned) with semantic checks: region affinity rules, tier predicates, model-variant compatibility matrix, and explicit fallback chains.
- A validation library used by the control-plane (Go) and by the console validator (TypeScript) exposing consistent messaging.
- A migration adapter that reads legacy rule shapes and emits v1->v2 transformation with a dry-run mode and automated correction suggestions.
- Unit and integration tests covering edge cases (empty fallbacks, circular fallbacks, cross-region hard constraints).
- CLI tool for ops to run bulk validation across customer configs and generate a remediation plan.
- Documentation: Confluence spec, sample configs, and a console lint panel for rule errors/warnings.

Constraints & Trade-offs:
- Backwards compatibility: We must avoid silent behavioral changes. The validator will default to warning for non-critical incompatibilities and error for safety-critical violations (e.g., no fallback defined for mandatory regions).
- Expressiveness vs. simplicity: DSL v1 will be intentionally conservative — composition primitives (AND/OR), explicit priority integers for fallbacks, and single-source-of-truth for model variants. Complex policies will be supported later once telemetry shows adoption.
- Runtime vs. compile-time checks: Some checks (model binary compatibility under quantization) require runtime metadata; validator will mark them as "deferred checks" with a link to runtime hooks.

Acceptance criteria:
1) Validator library runs against the current customer config corpus and reports zero safety-critical errors after migration guidance is applied.
2) Migration adapter can convert at least 95% of legacy rule shapes automatically (rest flagged with remediation steps).
3) Policy compiler rejects invalid configs with actionable messages and links to docs/console.
4) End-to-end testbench shows proper routing under simulated capacity pressure: regional affinity honored, tier isolation preserved, and fallback variants invoked in defined priority order.

Rollout plan:
- Week 1: Land schema + basic validator (dry-run) behind feature-flag; publish Confluence spec.
- Week 2: Run bulk validation across internal corpora and 10 pilot customers; iterate messages.
- Week 3: Ship migration adapter + ops CLI; begin console integration (lint panel).
- Week 4: Graduate validator to blocking mode for new configs; provide 30-day advisory period for legacy configs before cutover.

Notes on metrics to observe post-rollout:
- %configs passing validation (goal >95%)
- Number of policy compiler errors per day (expect initial spike, then drop)
- Incidents related to cross-region failovers (target reduction 80%)

Implementation hints:
- Reuse existing schema machinery from runtime-1.18 but add semantic layer for fallbacks and model compatibility.
- Validation library should produce both machine-readable diagnostics (code, path, severity) and human text for console/CLI.
- Keep migration adapter idempotent and log transformation diffs for audit.
